summary: Alexander Berzin is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned his B.A. from Rutgers and Princeton (~1961–1965) and a doctoral degree from Harvard (~1965–1972) under Masatoshi Nagatomi, later serving at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1972–1979).

Alexander Coburn Soper worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. Educated at Hamilton College and Princeton University (Ph.D. 1944), he taught at Bryn Mawr College, became a professor at New York University in 1960, and edited Artibus Asiae (1958–1993).

Alexander Cunningham specialized in Indology and archaeology. He studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary and under James Prinsep (1837–1838), founded the Archaeological Survey of India, and served as its first director (1861–1865) and director-general (1871–1885).
Alexander Duff was a scholar in religious studies and history and archaeology. He was educated at the University of Aberdeen and the University of St Andrews (~1821–1829).
Alexander Freiman studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1903–1907) and Christian Bartholomae (~1906–1907).

Alexander Gardner is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan in 2006 under Donald S. Lopez Jr., Janet Gyatso, and Robert H. Sharf, and held a post at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.
Alexander Hamilton was an Indologist. He served at the East India Company College as Professor of Sanskrit in 1806 and as Professor of Sanskrit and Hindu literature in 1808.
Alexander James O'Neill is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He was a PhD candidate at the University of Toronto and held a post as a research fellow at Taisho University.

Alexander Johnston worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied law at the University of Göttingen (~1792–1795) and Lincoln's Inn (~1795–1798), founded the Royal Asiatic Society, and served on the Executive Council of Ceylon (~1811–1819).

Alexander Kabanoff was a specialist in Japanology and Buddhist studies. By 2000, he was Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Alexander Lubotsky is an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Moscow State University and Leiden University (PhD ~1979–1987 under Robert S. P. Beekes), becoming Professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at Leiden in 1999.
Alexander Macmillan is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at SIT Graduate Institute under advisor Elizabeth Morrison (attested 2013).
Alexander Murray was a linguist. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1794–1800) and later held an academic post there (~1812–1813).

Alexander Ong Hsu specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2017) supervised by Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and held a teaching position at North Dakota State University.

Alexander Piatigorsky worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at Moscow State University (~1946–1951), he worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1957–1968) and taught at SOAS University of London, serving as Professor of the Ancient History of South Asia (1990–2001).
Alexander Rogers was an Indologist and historian. He studied at the East India Company College (~1843–1845) and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1845–1879).

Alexander Rödel is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2008) under the supervision of Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw.
Alexander W. Macdonald was a Tibetologist and religious studies scholar. He was a professor at Paris Nanterre University (~1970–1991) and was affiliated with the Musée de l'Homme (attested 1972).

Alexander Wynne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of Bristol (~1993–1996) and earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford (2000–2003) under Richard Gombrich.

Alexander Yiannopoulos works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and under supervisor Karin Myers (attested 2012–2017) as well as traditional teachers Khenpo Sherab Sangpo and Khenpo Sherab Dorje.
